8	/-!
9	# Pullback preserves quasi-coherence (Stacks 01BG, general morphism)
10	
11	For an arbitrary morphism of schemes `g : Y ⟶ X` and a quasi-coherent
12	`F : X.Modules`, the module pullback `g^* F = (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F`
13	is quasi-coherent (`pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom`).  This generalizes the
14	open-immersion case `isQuasicoherent_pullback_opens` (`CechTermAcyclic.lean`);
15	the previously-documented obstruction — `SheafOfModules.Presentation.map` only
16	transports a *global* presentation while quasi-coherence is *local* — is resolved
17	by localizing the pullback itself: over each member `U` of the quasi-coherence
18	cover of `X`, the restriction of `g^* F` to the preimage `W = g⁻¹(U)` is the
19	pullback of `F|_U` along the restricted morphism `g.resLE U W : W ⟶ U`
20	(the pullback pseudofunctor square `resLE_comp_ι`), and the *global* presentation
21	of `F|_U` transports along that restricted pullback.
22	
23	Two supporting facts are proved on the way:
24	
25	* `opensMap_final`: for any continuous map `φ`, the preimage functor
26	  `Opens.map φ` on opens is `Final` — the costructured comma poset
27	  `{U // d ≤ φ⁻¹(U)}` is nonempty (`⊤`) and `⊔`-directed, hence filtered.
28	* `pullbackObjUnitToUnit_isIso_hom`: consequently Mathlib's unit comparison
29	  `pullbackObjUnitToUnit` is an isomorphism for the module pullback along *any*
30	  scheme morphism, i.e. `g^* 𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪_Y` (`pullbackUnitIso`).
31	
32	These feed the flat-base-change RHS tilde leaf
33	`pushPullObj_coverInter_baseChanged_pushforward_iso_tilde`
34	(`CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`), which needs quasi-coherence of the
35	base-changed module `g'^* F` to apply the altitude-2 bridge
36	`pushPullObj_pushforward_iso_tilde` on the base-changed side.
37	-/
38

51	/-- The costructured comma category `StructuredArrow d (Opens.map φ)` — the poset of opens
52	`U` of the target with `d ≤ φ⁻¹(U)` — is filtered: it is nonempty (`U = ⊤`) and closed
53	under binary joins (`φ⁻¹` is monotone and preserves `⊔`), and it is thin, so parallel
54	pairs are automatically equalized. -/
55	instance opensMapStructuredArrow_isFiltered {T T' : TopCat.{u}} (φ : T ⟶ T')
56	    (d : Opens T) : IsFiltered (StructuredArrow d (Opens.map φ)) := by
57	  haveI hne : Nonempty (StructuredArrow d (Opens.map φ)) :=
58	    ⟨StructuredArrow.mk (Y := ⊤) (homOfLE (fun x _ => trivial))⟩
59	  haveI hfe : IsFilteredOrEmpty (StructuredArrow d (Opens.map φ)) := by
60	    constructor
61	    · intro j₁ j₂
62	      refine ⟨StructuredArrow.mk (Y := j₁.right ⊔ j₂.right)
63	          (j₁.hom ≫ (Opens.map φ).map (homOfLE le_sup_left)),
64	        StructuredArrow.homMk (homOfLE le_sup_left) rfl,
65	        StructuredArrow.homMk (homOfLE le_sup_right) (Subsingleton.elim _ _), trivial⟩
66	    · intro j₁ j₂ f g
67	      exact ⟨j₂, 𝟙 j₂, by apply StructuredArrow.hom_ext; exact Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
68	  constructor

70	/-- **The opens-preimage functor of any continuous map is final.**  Consequently global
71	sections of a pushforward along any scheme morphism compare correctly, and the module
72	pullback of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf (`pullbackObjUnitToUnit` is an
73	isomorphism, Mathlib's `[F.Final]` instance in `PullbackFree.lean`). -/
74	instance opensMap_final {T T' : TopCat.{u}} (φ : T ⟶ T') : (Opens.map φ).Final :=
75	  Functor.final_of_isFiltered_structuredArrow _

78	module pullback along any scheme morphism is an isomorphism (the underlying site functor
79	`Opens.map g.base` is final by `opensMap_final`). -/

91	/-! ## The per-slice presentation of a pullback -/
92	
93	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
94	/-- **The per-slice presentation of a pullback**: a presentation of `F.over A` induces a
95	presentation of the slice `(g^* F).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ A)`, for an arbitrary scheme morphism
96	`g : Y ⟶ X`.
97	
98	Route: let `W := g ⁻¹ᵁ A` and `gA := g.resLE A W : W ⟶ A` the restricted morphism.  The
99	X-side bridge (`presentationRestrictOfOver` at `W := A`) presents the full restriction
100	`F.restrict A.ι`; the restricted pullback `(pullback gA)` transports it
101	(`Presentation.map`, unit iso by `pullbackUnitIso`); the pullback pseudofunctor square
102	`gA ≫ A.ι = W.ι ≫ g` (`resLE_comp_ι`) identifies `(pullback gA).obj (F.restrict A.ι)`
103	with `(g^* F).restrict W.ι`; the V-side bridge engine (`modulesOverOpensEquivalence`
104	over `Y`) carries the presentation back to the over-slice. -/
105	noncomputable def presentationPullbackSliceOfOver {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
106	    (F : X.Modules) (A : X.Opens) (P : (F.over A).Presentation) :
107	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ A)).Presentation := by
108	  set W : Y.Opens := g ⁻¹ᵁ A with hW
109	  set G : Y.Modules := (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F with hG
110	  -- X-side: present the full restriction to `A`.
111	  letI P1 : (F.restrict A.ι).Presentation := presentationRestrictOfOver A F A P le_rfl
112	  -- The restricted morphism `W ⟶ A`.
113	  letI gA : W.toScheme ⟶ A.toScheme := g.resLE A W le_rfl
114	  -- Transport the presentation along the restricted pullback (colimit-preserving; unit ↦ unit).
115	  haveI hpc : Limits.PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
116	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback gA) := inferInstance
117	  letI P2 : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback gA).obj (F.restrict A.ι)).Presentation :=
118	    @SheafOfModules.Presentation.map _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ P1
119	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback gA) hpc (pullbackUnitIso gA).symm
120	  -- Identify with the restriction of the global pullback via the pseudofunctor square.
121	  have heq : gA ≫ A.ι = W.ι ≫ g := Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι g le_rfl
122	  letI e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback gA).obj (F.restrict A.ι) ≅ G.restrict W.ι :=
123	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback gA).mapIso
124	        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback A.ι).app F) ≪≫
125	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp gA A.ι).app F ≪≫
126	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr heq).app F ≪≫
127	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp W.ι g).app F).symm ≪≫
128	      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app G).symm
129	  letI P5 : (G.restrict W.ι).Presentation :=
130	    SheafOfModules.Presentation.ofIsIso.{u, u, u} e.hom P2
131	  -- V-side: carry the restriction presentation back to the over-slice through the engine.
132	  letI eV := modulesOverOpensEquivalence (X := Y) W
133	  letI P6 : (eV.inverse.obj (G.over W)).Presentation :=
134	    SheafOfModules.Presentation.ofIsIso.{u, u, u}
135	      (overOpensIsoRestrict W G).symm.hom P5
136	  letI ηV : eV.functor.obj (SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
137	      SheafOfModules.unit (Sheaf.over Y.ringCatSheaf W) :=
138	    overOpensFunctorUnitIso (X := Y) W
139	  letI P7 : (eV.functor.obj (eV.inverse.obj (G.over W))).Presentation :=
140	    P6.map eV.functor ηV.symm
141	  exact SheafOfModules.Presentation.ofIsIso.{u, u, u}
142	    (eV.counitIso.app (G.over W)).hom P7

148	-- Cover-local quasi-coherence repeatedly synthesizes right adjoints through the

151	/-- **Pullback preserves quasi-coherence** (Stacks 01BG, general-morphism case).  For an
152	arbitrary morphism of schemes `g : Y ⟶ X` and a quasi-coherent `F : X.Modules`, the module
153	pullback `g^* F` is quasi-coherent.
154	
155	Quasi-coherence is local (`SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.of_coversTop`): the preimages
156	under `g` of the quasi-coherence cover of `X` cover `Y`, and over each preimage the
157	per-slice obligation is `presentationPullbackSliceOfOver`. -/
158	theorem pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
159	    (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) :
160	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F).IsQuasicoherent := by
161	  obtain ⟨⟨q⟩⟩ := hF
162	  -- The preimages of the quasi-coherence cover of `X` cover `Y`.
163	  have hcov : (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y).CoversTop
164	      (fun i => g ⁻¹ᵁ q.X i) := by
165	    intro W x hx
166	    obtain ⟨U', fU, hf, hU'⟩ := q.coversTop ⊤ (g.base x) (by trivial)
167	    obtain ⟨i, ⟨gi⟩⟩ := hf
168	    refine ⟨W ⊓ (g ⁻¹ᵁ q.X i), homOfLE inf_le_left, ⟨i, ⟨homOfLE inf_le_right⟩⟩,
169	      ⟨hx, ?_⟩⟩
170	    exact (leOfHom gi) hU'
171	  -- Per-slice presentations through the restricted-pullback bridge.
172	  haveI hslice : ∀ i,
173	      (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ q.X i)).IsQuasicoherent := fun i =>
174	    (presentationPullbackSliceOfOver g F (q.X i) (q.presentation i)).isQuasicoherent
175	  exact SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.of_coversTop
176	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F) (fun i => g ⁻¹ᵁ q.X i) hcov
177

135	/-- **Flat base change has left-adjoint pullback**, hence `g^*` preserves finite
136	colimits (free: `g^* = pullback g` is a left adjoint). -/

140	/-- **Flat implies `g^*` is left-exact.**  This is not yet proved; what follows records the
141	reduction.
142	
143	By `SheafOfModules.pullbackIso`, the pullback factors as
144	`g^* ≅ forget ⋙ (PresheafOfModules.pullback φ.hom ⋙ PresheafOfModules.sheafification)`.
145	Two of the three factors preserve finite limits *in Mathlib already*:
146	* `SheafOfModules.forget` — `SheafOfModules.forgetPreservesFiniteLimits` (it is a right
147	  adjoint to sheafification);
148	* `PresheafOfModules.sheafification` — the instance in
149	  `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Presheaf/Sheafification.lean` (sheafification is a
150	  left-exact reflector; needs `HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat`, which holds for the scheme
151	  site since `X.Modules` is abelian).
152	
153	So the *only* irreducible content is that the **presheaf-level** pullback
154	`PresheafOfModules.pullback φ.hom` preserves finite limits when `g` is flat. Mathlib
155	defines this presheaf pullback purely as `(pushforward φ).leftAdjoint` with **no
156	pointwise description**; mathematically it is the inverse image `g⁻¹` (exact) followed
157	by extension of scalars along the flat ring map (left-exact, cf.
158	`ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat`), but neither this factorisation
159	nor its left-exactness is available.  Assembling the argument via `pullbackIso`
160	additionally requires the `sheafification`/`HasSheafify` instances for the scheme site. -/
161	instance pullback_preservesFiniteLimits (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g] :
162	    Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback g) := sorry

165	left-adjointness via `Functor.preservesHomologyOfExact`. -/
166	instance pullback_preservesHomology (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g] :
167	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).PreservesHomology := inferInstance

169	/-- **`g^*` commutes with Čech homology** (flat exactness, at the level of complexes).
170	A specialisation of `mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso` to `g^* = pullback g`, which is

204	/-! ## §3. The kernel–pullback comparison map -/
205	
206	/-- **The kernel–pullback comparison map** `g'^*(ker q) ⟶ ker (g'^* q)`
207	(the abstract `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison` at the module pullback
208	functor; the pullback preserves zero morphisms, being a left adjoint —
209	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction` — between abelian categories).
210	It is characterised by `κ ≫ ker(g'^*q).ι = g'^*(ker q .ι)`
211	(`kernelComparison_comp_ι`).  `Scheme.Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
212	(blueprint `lem:relative_divisor_base_change`) proves it is an isomorphism
213	when the cokernel of `ker q ⟶ E` is flat over the base of a cartesian
214	square. -/
215	noncomputable def Modules.pullbackKernelComparison
216	    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) {E F : X.Modules} (q : E ⟶ F) :
217	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj (Limits.kernel q) ⟶
218	      Limits.kernel ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map q) :=
219	  kernelComparison q (Scheme.Modules.pullback g')

A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is flat if for each affine `U ⊆ Y` and
`V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U`, the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)` is flat. This is equivalent to
asking that all stalk maps are flat (see `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`).

asking that all stalk maps are flat (see `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`).
-/
@[mk_iff]
class Flat (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop where
  flat_appLE (f) :
    ∀ {U : Y.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen U) {V : X.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U),
      (f.appLE U V e).hom.Flat

  HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff

  MorphismProperty.comp_mem _ f g hf hg

  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance

instance (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Y.Opens) [Flat f] : Flat (f ∣_ V) :=
  IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.restrict ‹_› V

15:Let `S` and `R` be sheaves of rings over sites `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` respectively.

17:let `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` be a morphism

21:`pullback.{v} φ : SheafOfModules.{v} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} R`

23:under suitable assumptions, and prove that the pullback of (pre)sheaves of
24:modules commutes with the sheafification.

27:similar pseudofunctor-like properties of the `pullback` functors.

name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
